No stray test DB files got committed to tracking (already gitignored). Both `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` pass cleanly.

## Summary

The vulnerability was in `app/Http/Controllers/ProfileController.ts:update()` — it parsed the raw request body with a type assertion (`this.request.json<ProfileInput>()`) and passed it straight through to `User.forceUpdate()`, which bypasses both validation and the model's mass-assignment allowlist (`fillable`). The project already had an unused `ProfileUpdateSchema` (Zod, in `app/Http/Validators/ProfileValidator.ts`) mirroring the registration rules for `name`/`email`/`password`.

I wired it in: the controller now calls `this.validateBody(ProfileUpdateSchema)` (the same pattern `RegisterController` uses), which rejects malformed email, empty name, and too-short passwords with a 422 that flows into the existing `form.errors.name/email/password` handling on the frontend — no frontend changes were needed since `resources/js/pages/profile/Edit.tsx` already reads those fields via Inertia's `useForm().errors`. I also swapped `User.forceUpdate` for the mass-assignment-safe `User.update`, and built its payload explicitly from only the validated `name`/`email`/`password` fields, so extra client-supplied fields like `id` or `passwordHash` are never read or written.

I added `tests/ProfileController.test.ts` covering: a valid update persisting, rejection of a malformed email/empty name/short password (with the account left unchanged), and confirmation that extraneous fields (`id`, `passwordHash`) sent in the request body are ignored. `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` both pass (7/7).
